## Bio

I'm an analyst, and I do the analytics engineering the analysis depends on. I build the systems that make numbers trustworthy at scale — the metric definitions, the data models, and the governance underneath them, not just the dashboard sitting on top. A report is only as good as the data behind it, and that layer is the work.

Over 12+ years I've done this from both chairs. At Lowe's ecommerce arm I proposed the business intelligence function, hired its first analysts, and ran a team of six through building the data warehouse and the reporting stack that supported $10M+ in revenue. At Philips Healthcare I led BI and analytics programs across a global manufacturing operation — ten factories, three continents, 200+ stakeholders in eight countries — standardizing 200+ Critical Data Elements into a common data model, harmonizing KPI frameworks across those ten factories, and taking $80K a year out of the reporting estate through rationalization. That was leadership through influence rather than reporting lines, which is the harder version of the job.

The craft is current. Every module in the Cascadia portfolio was built in 2026 to my specification: I set the architecture, the data models, the metric definitions and the validation gates, and directed the build. The code is public on GitHub — governed data models, matching rules documented as deliverables in their own right, and validation suites that fail the build rather than ship a number I can't defend.

I ran a team, and I am looking for an individual contributor seat on purpose. I want more hands-on time with the new AI tooling inside a working organization before I take another manager title. I kept my own book of work the whole time I was managing; staying close to the data and the tools is the part I do not want to give up.

---

## Selected outcomes

- **Governed data at enterprise scale.** I standardized 200+ Critical Data Elements and common data model definitions across a global manufacturing platform, enforcing semantic consistency across systems that had none.
- **Harmonized metrics across ten factories.** I replaced site-by-site KPI variants with one trusted framework, 17 automated KPIs and 21 new T4 KPIs, so leadership could compare plants on definitions that actually matched.
- **Eliminated 100+ hours a week of manual reporting.** I moved disconnected spreadsheets and point-in-time extracts into automated, governed dashboards.
- **Zero audit findings** in a regulated medical-device data environment, with access-controlled handling of sensitive data.
- **Took $80K a year out of the reporting estate.** I ran the BI rationalization that governed refresh rates, usage, ownership and access, and removed the duplicate and abandoned reporting it found.
- **Founded a BI function.** I proposed the department at Lowe's/ATG Stores, hired its foundational team, and managed six analysts and developers through the build of the data warehouse, the KPI definitions and the stewardship model.

## Skills

The split below is the same division of labour described in "How I built this."

- **Tools I work in directly:** Power BI (data modeling, Power Query/M), Tableau, Qlik, SAP BusinessObjects, advanced Excel, SQL (queries, joins, views, transformations), SAP HANA, dimensional/star-schema & semantic modeling, ETL/ELT & data integration, data governance & quality
- **Tools I specify against and validate:** Python, DuckDB, dbt, Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Azure data platforms
- **KPI & frameworks:** KPI development & governance, leading/lagging indicator frameworks, Critical Data Elements & common data models, BI rationalization
- **Domains:** healthcare (manufacturing, quality, pharmacy/public-health), ecommerce & retail, workforce/staffing, financial analytics
- **Program & enablement:** BI function ownership, analytics program & portfolio management, Agile (Scrumban) / Scrum Master, stakeholder management across eight countries, self-service enablement, mentoring analysts
